newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: MOORE IN QUESTION OVER SHAREHOLDINGS

The Opposition says Industry Minister John Moore is in a vulnerable position following revelations of his shareholdings. This follows the resignation of former Assistant Treasurer Jim Short over shares he held affecting his portfolio, and questions over Treasurer Peter Costello's wife's shareholdings.
Mr Moore holds more than 40,000 shares in Bligh Ventures, a company with interests the petrol and computing industries.
He's sold 5,000 of the shares, but hasn't been able to find a buyer at market price for another 43,000.
Shadow Treasurer, Gareth Evans, told ABC Radio, that Mr Moore, should divest his shares, regardless of the price they'll fetch.
He says Mr Moore is choosing to hang on to the shares for a price he's in the position of influencing.
OPPOSITION WARNS OF LOWER COMPETITION
The Federal Opposition says any further banking mergers could lead to the dramatic reduction in the amount of retail banking outlets throughout the country.
That follows the announced merger between the St George and Advance banks.

Treasury spokesman, Gareth Evans, says allowing competition to drop to unacceptable levels will have serious implications for many Australians in terms of employment, and services to country towns and regions.
FEARS THAT ABC WILL BE MARGINALISED
The man appointed to review the ABC says most of the public submissions he's received have expressed fear that the ABC may be marginalised.
Bob Mansfield has told ABC radio he's received about 11-and-a-half thousand submissions to date.
He says the core elements of the ABC such as services to rural and remote areas, news and current affairs, Australian content, and localism, are not under threat.
Mr Mansfield says the biggest fear people have is that the ABC will end up a follower of the commercial stations.
LANGE WARNS OF LOW WAGE ECONOMY
A Brisbane conference has been told that Australia could follow the path of New Zealand if it moves to deregulate the labour market.

Former New Zealand Prime Minister David Lange told the Society of Certified Practising Accountants, Australia should learn from New Zealand's experience, where labour deregulation has failed to improve productivity.
Mr Lange said there's a danger New Zealand could end up as a predominantly low-wage economy.
KOALAS LINK TO HEART DISEASE IN HUMANS
Researchers believe one of Australia's favorite native animals could one day advance the fight against heart disease in humans.
University of Technology scientists are investigating a possible link between human heart disease and chlamydia in koalas.
Peter Timms says a link has already been established between a strain of the disease in koalas, and respiratory infections and pneumonia in humans.
CARNE HOT PROPERTY AFTER BRONCOS DUMPING
Two Brisbane Broncos stars will be in Adelaide today for talks on a possible move to the Adelaide Rams for next years Super League competition.
Internationals Willie Carne and Kerrod Walters will hold discussions with Rams officials and inspect the clubs new headquarters.
The Rams aren't, however, the only club wanting Carne's services.
The brilliant winger will be in Perth later this week for talks with the Western Reds, and the Canberra Raiders have expressed their interest in gaining his signature.
-- Reuters Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
